statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Registries and Online Services – Corporate Online
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be presented in Latin script; Arabic numerals are permitted; French and English characters are accepted; non-Latin script names must be transliterated into Latin script and accompanied by a certified translation. The name must include a legal element indicating limited liability, such as 'Limited Partnership' or 'L.P.'. Symbols and punctuation are restricted to ampersand or similar corporate-legal characters.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name is rejected, the applicant may file a Name Reconsideration Request through BC Registries and Online Services or by written submission to the Corporate Registry. The written request must identify the rejected name, the ground of rejection, and arguments justifying approval. If reconsideration remains unsuccessful, the applicant may apply to the Supreme Court of British Columbia for judicial review under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 241. Name reservations cannot be extended beyond 56 days; a new reservation request must be filed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted solely for the registered address and records-delivery address of the limited partnership. A physical service address with an identifiable individual is required for service of process. A remote mailbox-only address will not satisfy the commercial-substance test for manufacturing activities, tax treaty access, or Health Canada device licensing; a substantial physical presence in British Columbia is required for ISIC 3250 aligner manufacturing and thermoforming operations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate: approximately 6% per fiscal year for a registered LP not claiming tax incentives, rising to approximately 12–15% where SR&ED or medical-device tax credits are claimed. Unannounced inspections by BC Registry compliance staff are rare but possible if the registered office is suspected to be non-operational or virtual-only.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnership Act, RSBC 1996, c. 347, ss. 7-14 (registration, contribution, general partner liability); Partnership Act, RSBC 1996, c. 348, s. 3 (definition); Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c. 57, s. 38 (adopted for name reservation rules)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registry Services, Corporate Registry, Ministry of Citizens' Services, Victoria, British Columbia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership (Form LP-1) and Notice of Registered Office and Agent (Form LP-2)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a British Columbia limited partnership; capital may be fixed at zero or nominal amount in the partnership agreement. No escrow account is required; contributions may be in cash or property and are governed by the Limited Partnership Act and the partnership agreement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The undersigned general partner, acting in accordance with the partnership agreement and the Limited Partnership Act, RSBC 1996, c. 347, hereby resolves: (1) to subscribe for and accept the initial capital contributions set forth in Schedule A; (2) to adopt the registered office at [address] and to appoint [name] as agent for service in British Columbia; (3) to appoint [name] as chief financial officer and head of manufacturing operations for the Limited Partnership; (4) to open Canadian banking accounts and authorize signatory limits; and (5) to direct counsel to complete all filings, licenses, and regulatory registrations necessary for Good Standing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search and Reservation for British Columbia Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registry Services, Corporate Registry online via BC Registries and Online Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS-style name search through BC Registry Services to ensure the proposed limited partnership name is distinguishable from existing corporate, LLP, and LP names. Submit a name reservation request online, paying the reservation fee. If the name contains 'Medical' or 'Aligners', add a consent/clearance letter for regulated medical device terminology. Retain the reservation report for 56 days.
required_dossiers: Completed Name Search Request
Proposed limited partnership name and optional assumed name
Signed name clearance letter if using regulated terms
Payment method for reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a Request for Reconsideration with BC Registry within 21 days, provide supporting legal citations, and amend the proposed name with a distinguishing element.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form LP-1 online or in paper, listing general partners and limited partners, registered office, agent for service, and capital contribution summary. Pay filing fee and submit executed partnership agreement extract if requested. Obtain Certificate of Registration and Good Standing confirmation.
required_dossiers: Form LP-1 executed by general partner
Consent of each general partner
Original partnership agreement or execution extract
Valid name reservation report
Registered office and agent appointment (Form LP-2)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, file an amended Form LP-1 with BC Registry within 30 days and pay the correction fee; attach an affidavit explaining the inadvertent omission and curative amendment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of Registered Office and Agent for Service in British Columbia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and file Notice of Registered Office and Agent for Service in BC. The registered office must be a physical address in BC and not a post office box. The agent must be a Canadian resident or a licensed BC extra-provincial company authorized to accept service.
required_dossiers: Form LP-2
Consent of agent for service
Proof of BC street address and civic address
Agent's legal name and contact details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the agent refuses or address is rejected, submit a replacement Form LP-2 within 14 days and provide a signed consent by the new agent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and BC Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a Business Number and register for GST/HST, payroll deductions, and provincial employer programs through CRA Business Registration Online. Register for BC employer payroll program and, if applicable, BC PST. Since the entity is a limited partnership, obtain partnership identification number and file necessary elections.
required_dossiers: BC Certificate of Registration
Partnership agreement
General partner's Canadian identification or corporate registration
Business address and banking details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA blocks registration pending identity confirmation, submit authenticated partnership certificate, general partner consent, and CRA confidentiality authorization; escalate within 14 days by contacting CRA Objection Team.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Zoning Clearance for Manufacturing Premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City/Regional District Local Government Business Licensing Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit municipal business licence application for light manufacturing of dental clear aligner sheets. Obtain zoning certificate confirming premises are zoned industrial M-1 or equivalent, and submit floor plan showing thermoforming equipment, trimming cells, and quality control rooms. Pay application fee and annual licence fee.
required_dossiers: BC LP registration certificate
Zoning certificate or land use approval from municipality
Floor plan and equipment layout
Hazardous waste and chemical storage inventory
Civic address and building occupancy permit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality requires variances, file a minor variance application with the Municipal Board of Adjustment and provide a public notice; if licence is denied, appeal to the Local Government Appeal Board within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Health Canada Medical Devices Directorate and WorkSafeBC (Occupational Health and Safety)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Medical Device Establishment Licence (Canada) under Food and Drugs Act and Medical Devices Regulations (SOR/98/282)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy, Environmental Assessment Office
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Screening/Registration (Condition Exemption) under the Environmental Management Act and the Reviewable Projects Regulation; not a full EIA for typical thermoforming operations below 50,000 m² of production area.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges to sewer must meet municipal industrial waste bylaw limits; thermoforming emissions must comply with B.C. Reg. 30/2012 (Procedure Regulation) and the Multi-Sector Air Pollutants Regulation where applicable, including VOC stack concentration limit of 20 mg/m³ at 25°C (reference) and particulate filter threshold of 30 mg/m³ for plastic pyrolysis residues. Solid plastic waste must be stored covered and disposed through certified recycler; hazardous solvents must be managed under the Hazardous Waste Regulation (B.C. Reg. 63/88).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Prior to operation, obtain Fire Safety Permit under the BC Fire Code, structural load assessment certified by a licensed professional engineer for thermoforming machinery, and WorkSafeBC clearance confirming compliance with OHS Guideline G.D2.13 for plastic manufacturing (emergency stops, guarding, lockout/tagout) and sanitary registration for medical-device production.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) via My Business Account and Business Registration Online (BRO); British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST) is administered by the BC Ministry of Finance through eTaxBC; exports are declared through the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) Canadian Export Reporting System.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The BC limited partnership obtains a statutory 9-digit CRA Business Number (BN) in the partnership name. The general partner, or an authorized Canadian representative, files Form RC1 or registers online through BRO and selects the GST/HST program account. The filing must be accompanied by the BC certificate of limited partnership, the executed partnership agreement, and the identity and address details of all partners, including non-resident foreign corporate partners. There is no minimum capital requirement, and non-resident ownership is permitted. A non-resident partnership without a Canadian establishment may still register for GST/HST where it carries on business in Canada or makes registrable taxable supplies; in such case CRA may require a Canadian agent for service and a mailing address in Canada. BC PST requires a separate registration through eTaxBC before the partnership makes taxable retail sales or leases in BC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible: A Canadian limited partnership is fiscally transparent for Canadian income tax purposes; income is computed at the partnership level under the Income Tax Act and allocated to partners. For GST/HST purposes, the partnership is itself a separate registrable person (the Excise Tax Act definition of person includes a partnership), so the same LP may hold both a partnerships BN/GST account and remain remitted at the partner level for income tax. There is no separate entity-level income tax at the LP level and no territorial or tax-exempt zone classification applies to the BC activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not have a US-style check-the-box elective classification regime; classification is statutory. Available statutory elections and mechanisms for a cross-border BC LP: (i) an election under the Income Tax Act to treat a foreign entity that is opaque under foreign corporate law as a partnership for Canadian partners; (ii) designation of a nominated or elected partnership member for GST/HST registration, administration, and input tax credit claims; (iii) an election to adopt a non-calendar partnership fiscal period for Canadian income tax; (iv) the Excise Tax Act mechanism permitting a partner to act as agent for the partnership in GST/HST matters; and (v) automatic application of Canada's hybrid mismatch arrangement rules, which deny deductions or recharacterize passthrough payments when an entity is treated differently in another jurisdiction; no elective carve-out is provided for hybrid mismatches.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax): British Columbia applies the 5% federal GST separately; BC does not participate in the Harmonized Sales Tax and imposes a separate 7% Provincial Sales Tax (PST) on taxable goods and services consumed in BC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold: total consideration for taxable supplies made in Canada, including zero-rated exports, in a single calendar quarter or over the immediately preceding four consecutive calendar quarters triggers mandatory GST/HST registration. Registration is required once the threshold is crossed, with liability applying from the first supply that caused the threshold to be exceeded. BC PST registration is required before making any taxable retail sales or leases in BC without regard to a revenue threshold; zero-rated export sales of dental aligner sheets delivered outside BC are excluded from PST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory digital stamping, or government API invoice pre-clearance regime applies in Canada. CRA operates a voluntary Pan-Canadian e-invoicing framework built on the Peppol network for B2B and B2G transactions. Electronic GST/HST return filing via NETFILE or EDI is mandatory for registrants with annual taxable supplies exceeding CAD 1.5M, and electronic remittance through CRA My Business Account is required for such registrants. BC PST returns must be filed electronically through eTaxBC. No statutory IT or API clearance requirement applies to the export of thermoformed dental aligner sheets.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act. Section 6 zero-rates tangible personal property, such as clear aligner thermoform sheets, supplied to a non-resident purchaser and exported by or on behalf of the supplier from Canada to a destination outside Canada in the ordinary course of commercial activity within the prescribed export time frame. Section 7 zero-rates services supplied to a non-resident recipient when the services are not performed in connection with real property situated in Canada or tangible personal property situated in Canada. The BC limited partnership must be a GST/HST registrant at the time of supply to claim the 0% rate and must retain evidence of export as prescribed by the Excise Tax Act and the Exporters of Goods Regulations. Exports physically delivered outside British Columbia are also outside the scope of BC PST.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (B13A or electronic export declaration EED) filed through the CBSA Canadian Export Reporting System
Carrier-issued bill of lading or air waybill evidencing the foreign destination and the actual export date
Commercial invoice including the declared HS classification (e.g., 9018.49 or 3920.9) and the packing list
Purchase order or executed supply agreement with the non-resident customer
PST exemption or billing documentation confirming direct delivery outside BC where required for BC PST purposes
Bank remittance evidence, comprising inward credit advice or an FX conversion record confirming payment received in CAD within the repatriation window
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and CBSA audit export substantiation against physical exit of the goods from Canada. Incomplete, inconsistent, or fraudulent export documentation causes retrospective disallowance of zero-rating and reassessment of GST at 5% with interest and late-remittance penalties; falsified export declarations trigger the Excise Tax Act gross-negligence penalty of the greater of CAD 250 and 25% of the net tax understated, a seven-year reassessment window for misrepresentation, and criminal liability under ETA section 327 with, on indictment, a fine of up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to five years. BC PST audits may additionally claw back uncollected PST where goods are found to have been consumed in BC, with penalties under the Provincial Sales Tax Act. The complete evidence bundle, including the commercial invoice, export declaration, bill of lading, and inward remittance evidence, is therefore a statutory, audit-critical condition of the export zero-rating claim.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada / Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) / Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current and capital account convertibility and has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations; the Canadian dollar (CAD) floats freely, and there are no exchange-control restrictions on dividend, interest, or royalty remittances by a British Columbia limited partnership. Cross-border payments are subject only to FINTRAC large-transfer reporting and Part XIII non-resident withholding tax where applicable; no ex-ante approval from the Bank of Canada is required for either inbound capital contributions or outbound profit distributions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None — Canada imposes no statutory surrender, repatriation, or conversion obligation on export proceeds. Export receipts may be retained in CAD or foreign currency at the entity's discretion; however, transactions over C$10,000 crossing the border must be reported under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, and trade documentation (commercial invoices, bills of lading) must substantiate exports declared to Statistics Canada and the Canada Border Services Agency.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium — Foreign digital EMIs such as Wise, Airwallex, and Payoneer may operate as Money Service Businesses (MSBs) only if registered with FINTRAC; their Canadian footprint and Bank of Canada settlement access are indirect, and they do not qualify as primary licensed deposit-taking institutions. Feasibility is Medium (viable as supporting cross-border payout and FX remittance rails, but not for escrowed capital, regulatory license deposits, or Letters of Credit, which require a Schedule I bank relationship).
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors of the General Partner and all individuals holding >25% of the Limited Partnership must complete a CIP (Customer Identification Process). An in-person or bank-approved video KYC interview is standard for non-resident directors; face-to-face interview is normally mandated unless the financial institution accepts enhanced remote verification through a Canadian or recognized foreign bank reference letter and certified identity documents. Evidence of physical business presence in British Columbia (registered office, lease, or shared office agreement) materially increases onboarding speed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex multi-tier LP ownership with non-resident limited partners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Certificate of Limited Partnership from BC Registry, executed Limited Partnership Agreement, full organizational chart, UBO register (25%+ ownership), source-of-wealth declarations, and certified passports/address proofs of all principals.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors or General Partner domiciled outside Canada
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank-to-bank reference from home jurisdiction, tax residence certificates, proof of physical Canadian registered office, corporate registry abstracts, and a Canadian legal opinion confirming the LP validly exists and is authorized to bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume inbound wires deemed inconsistent with orthodontics trade
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master supply agreements, pro-forma invoices, bills of lading and Cargo Control Documents (Canada), customs entry summaries, unit-cost/price validation for clear aligner thermoformed sheets, and vendor/customer KYC profiles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Aggregated platform revenue cleared via Stripe payout to LP bank account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Stripe merchant agreement and settlement reports, platform-payout reconciliation ledger, credit-card deposit history, refund and chargeback policy, and a segregated reconciliation of platform proceeds against disbursements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP or enhanced-risk jurisdiction exposure in investor base
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP questionnaire, source-of-funds/source-of-wealth reports, sanctions screening clearance, notarized declarations, independent AML legal opinion, and evidence of economic nexus in British Columbia (manufacturing assets, payroll, real property).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections flow via SWIFT MT103 to the LP's Canadian bank account using purpose code (e.g., ISO 20022 purpose 'CAPT' for capital payment / 'INVC' for intercompany invoice) and referencing the LP's Legal Entity Identifier (LEI). For transfers above C$10,000, FINTRAC reporting applies; the beneficiary bank will verify KYC before credit. CAD funding may alternatively be routed via Payments Canada Lynx for domestic large-value settlement. Documentary verification requires a board-approved capital contribution resolution, updated LP register, and, for foreign investors, an FX/tax clearance confirming no federal approval is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for raw polymer granules, thermoforming tooling, and Contract Manufacturing Organization (CMO) services are cleared via SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers and, where credit-backed, through Commercial Letters of Credit issued as SWIFT MT700/MT707 from the LP's issuing bank to supplier banks. CAD-denominated domestic supplier payments use Payments Canada EFT/ACH or Lynx; USD-derived Stripe payouts are settled via ACH-like automated clearing and repatriated through spot conversions; FX conversion is executed through the FX treasury account at the Canadian bank rather than the EMI rail to preserve regulatory traceability.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD spot and plain-vanilla FX forwards (tenor ≤12 months, extendable to 24 months with board approval)
Cross-currency swaps (CAD/USD and CAD/EUR) for matching long-term machinery leases or US-dollar trade payables
Vanilla FX options (call/put and zero-premium collars) traded with Schedule I bank counterparties under ISDA/CSA documentation
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for settling embedded exposures in non-convertible currencies (e.g., CNY/INR amounts flowing from certain APAC aligner distributors)
Exchange-traded CAD futures and options on CME for margin-efficient hedging of large USD receivables

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Limited Partnership Annual Report (Form LP-AR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: British Columbia Registrar of Companies (BC Registries and Online Services)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of the date of registration in British Columbia
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of CAD 50 in addition to the CAD 30 annual fee; failure to file for two consecutive years triggers administrative strike-off of the limited partnership from the BC register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return (T5013 Summary and T5013 Slips)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal year-end, due March 31 of the following year; for a non-calendar fiscal period, due no later than the later of March 31 and seven months after the fiscal period end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of CAD 25 per partner per month, minimum CAD 100 and maximum CAD 2,500, plus interest; failure to file may also cause CRA to disallow partnership deductions and impose additional compliance measures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Canada Revenue Agency T5013 Slips Distribution to Partners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - each partner must receive a slip
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 following the partnership's calendar year-end, or by the T5013 filing due date for non-calendar fiscal periods
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to provide slips to partners may result in CRA penalties under subsection 162(7.1) of the Income Tax Act, up to CAD 2,500 for late or missing slips.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit requirement under the BC Partnership Act for limited partnerships. A mandatory independent audit arises only if the LP is a reporting issuer under securities legislation, if required by the partnership agreement, or as a contractual condition imposed by lenders or significant investors.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian private enterprises may adopt IFRS or Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE). A limited partnership may prepare financial statements under ASPE, IFRS, or tax-basis records acceptable for CRA reporting; ASPE is the common default for a private BC LP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: British Columbia does not maintain a public UBO register for limited partnerships. The BC annual report requires the general partner to confirm the registered office and current partner information. Any transfer of a partnership interest must be recorded in the LP's internal register and, if a general partner changes, filed with the BC Registrar as an amended declaration. This annual filing and internal updating together serve as the de facto beneficial ownership confirmation for the LP.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners (names, addresses, capital contributions, and transfers)
Register of General Partners (names and addresses)
Minute Book (copies of annual declarations, amended declarations, and partnership resolutions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150 - 450 per year (CAD 200 - 600) depending on the BC corporate agent and registered-office services selected
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not statutorily required; if voluntarily engaged, approximately USD 2,250 - 6,000 (CAD 3,000 - 8,000) for a mid-sized BC limited partnership

stage_6.entry_description: Partnership legal name, business address, Business Number (BN) program account RT account for GST/HST if registered, fiscal period start/end dates, and the BC Registry incorporation number.
stage_6.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify each non-resident partner and their residency country; the return must be completed in English or French and report the partnership's Canadian-source gross revenue and expenses.
